title: briefing report or deck, format 1
description: A briefing report ("blocks") or slide deck ("slides") as JSON: the same blocks and options as in Python. Check it with briefing.validate(spec, data).

block.description: Any block but a Page (pages only go at the top level).

Text.description: Markdown text block (CommonMark plus pipe tables).

text.description: Markdown; common leading indentation is removed.

file.description: Path to a `.md` file to read instead of `text`.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

columns.description: Number of grid columns, a whole number of 1 or more.

widths.description: Relative column widths, positive numbers, one per column (e.g. `[2, 1]`).

valign.description: Vertical alignment of the cells: `"top"`, `"center"` or `"bottom"`.

min_width.description: The narrowest a cell may be, such as `"16rem"` (or a number of pixels): as many cells per row as fit, up to `columns` when it is above 1. Not with `widths`.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

Card.description: A framed box with a title, around blocks stacked in one column.

title.description: The card's heading, with inline Markdown as in captions.

icon.description: A short mark before the title, such as an emoji (up to 8 characters).

tags.description: Pills at the bottom of the card: texts or Chip.

link.description: A block or heading link such as `"page/name"` (see the links guide): the whole card leads there. Needs a `title`, which is the link's text.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

Select.description: Tab or dropdown selector — shows one child block at a time.

style.description: How the tabs look: a TabStyle (layout, size, variant…). Tabs only.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

Toggle.description: Collapsible container — hidden by default, expanded on click.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: The clickable title (`"Details"` when omitted).

name.description: Stable block id; `save_image` / `save_pdf` accept it as `page=`.

BigNumber.description: KPI display block — shows a headline metric with optional change indicator.

change.description: Optional change to show under the value, e.g. `"+3%"`.

is_upward_change.description: The arrow: `True` shows ▲, `False` shows ▼, `None` shows no arrow.

is_positive_intent.description: The colour: `True` is green (good news), `False` is red (bad news). Leave it `None` and the colour follows the arrow (▲ green, ▼ red); with neither flag the change is shown neutral, in the theme's muted colour.

prev_value.description: The value to compare with: briefing computes the change, its arrow and its colour (instead of `change`, `is_upward_change` and `is_positive_intent`). Needs a numeric `value`.

change_as.description: How a computed change is shown: `"percent"` (`+10.5%`), `"absolute"` (the difference, in `format`) or `"points"` (the difference of two rates in percentage points, `-0.3 pt`).

higher_is_better.description: With `prev_value`: `True` shows a rise in green, `False` a fall (churn, cost, latency).

format.description: How `value` is shown: a format string such as `"{:,.0f}"`, `"$ {:.1f}M"` or `"{:.1%}"`, or a function.

sparkline.description: A short series of numbers drawn as a trend line under the value (a list, a Series or an array); missing values leave gaps.

accent.description: A colour stripe on the card's left edge: `"up"`, `"down"` or `"accent"` (the theme's colours) or a CSS colour.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

title.description: Optional bold title above the message.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

Chips.description: A wrapping row of pills: labels, tags, or values that rose or fell.

items.description: The pills: text, or Chip for a tooltip or a colour.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

Legend.description: One legend for the blocks that share a Scale, such as a page of calendars.

scale.description: A Scale with a `domain`: the values its colours stand for, or the categories of a named palette (one swatch each).

title.description: A short line above the legend, with inline Markdown as in captions.

events.description: Dates to list, as `CalendarHeatmap(events=)` takes them, with their colours.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

Banner.description: Markdown text over a background image: a report cover, a section opener or a social card.

image.description: A file path, or the image bytes (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG).

text_position.description: 0–100: where the text column begins (`side="right"`) or ends (`side="left"`), in percent of the banner's width.

opacity.description: 0–100: how much the veil covers the image under the text: 100 is a plain text panel, around 80 leaves the image faintly visible. No readability warning is given at any value; that is your call.

side.description: `"right"` (text on the right, image clear on the left) or `"left"`. Ignored when `fade=False`.

fade.description: `True` fades the veil in over 20 % of the width before the text; `False` covers the whole image with one veil at `opacity`.

height.description: CSS height such as `"16rem"` (default) or a number of pixels.

focus.description: `(x, y)` in percent: the point of the image kept in view when it is cropped.

alt.description: A description of the image; by default it is decorative.

kicker.description: One short line of plain text above `text`, smaller and in the theme's muted colour, such as `"Data through Nov 20, 2026"`. Escaped, never Markdown.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

Image.description: A picture: a PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG file, embedded in the report.

image.description: A file path, or the image's bytes (PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP or SVG).

alt.description: What the image shows, for readers who can't see it; by default the caption. With neither, the image is decorative.

width.description: A CSS width such as `"60%"` or `"20rem"`, or a number of pixels.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

Attachment.description: A file readers download from the report: any file, some bytes, or a dataframe as CSV.

file.description: A file path (any type), bytes (then `filename` is needed), or a dataframe, which downloads as CSV in the format of `DataTable`'s CSV button: raw values, UTF-8 with a byte-order mark.

filename.description: The name the file downloads as; by default the file's own name, or for a dataframe the block's `name` (else `data`) with `.csv`.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: The link's text (by default the file name), and its tab title inside a `Select`.

figure.description: A Plotly, Altair, Matplotlib (or Seaborn / Plotnine) or Bokeh figure.

caption.description: Optional caption shown below the chart.

responsive.description: Let the chart fill the width of its container. Size the figure in its plotting library, e.g. Matplotlib's `figsize=(w, h)`.

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

Table.description: Static HTML table rendered from a dataframe or a pandas Styler.

data.description: A dataframe (as for DataTable) or a pandas `Styler`, kept as-is.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

DataTable.description: Interactive, sortable and searchable table rendered from a pandas DataFrame.

df.description: The data: pandas, polars, pyarrow, anything with the dataframe interchange protocol, or a dict of columns.

max_rows.description: Rows beyond this are dropped with a warning.

formats.description: How to show a column's values: `{"revenue": "€ {:,.0f}", "share": "{:.1%}", "day": "{:%d %b %Y}"}`, Python format strings (as in pandas' `Styler.format`) or functions. Cells still sort by their raw value; missing values stay empty.

links.description: Columns whose cells link somewhere: `{"doi": "https://doi.org/{}", "title": "{url}"}`, a URL template where `{}` is the cell's value and `{url}` the value of the column `url` in the same row. Only `http(s)://` and `mailto:` URLs make links (anything else stays text, with a warning); they open in a new tab.

wrap.description: Columns whose text wraps onto several lines, instead of making the table scroll sideways: a list of column names, or `True` for every column.

download.description: Put a "CSV" button above the table: it downloads the rows matching the reader's search, in their order, with their raw values (not the formatted text), as a file named after the table's `name` or caption.

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

language.description: Language for syntax highlighting (any Pygments lexer name, e.g. `"python"`, `"sql"`); an unknown language is shown as plain text.

lab.DataDive.description: Interactive dot explorer — similar to Google's Facets Dive.

df.description: The data, as any dataframe briefing accepts.

x.description: Column on the X axis at first (the viewer can change it).

y.description: Column on the Y axis at first.

color.description: Column that colours the dots at first.

facet_row.description: Accepted but not drawn yet (a warning says so); planned for DataDive v2.

facet_col.description: Accepted but not drawn yet (a warning says so); planned for DataDive v2.

colors.description: A Scale for the dots' colours, so they match the other blocks of the report. A categorical scale colours the categories it names (others take the theme's palette); a numeric one colours numbers and dates. Without it, categories take the theme's palette and numbers a ramp to its accent.

max_rows.description: Larger frames are sampled down to this many rows, with a warning.

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

lab.CalendarHeatmap.description: GitHub-style calendar heatmap: one cell per day, weeks as columns.

df.description: The data, as any dataframe briefing accepts (pandas, polars, pyarrow…).

date.description: Column holding the date or timestamp of each row.

value.description: Column to aggregate per day; `None` counts the rows.

group.description: Column to split by: one calendar per group, stacked, on one shared colour scale.

views.description: Only `("days",)`; the hour view was removed in 0.5.0 (use TimeHeatmap).

tz.description: A time zone such as `"America/Montreal"`. Converts timezone-aware timestamps only; naive timestamps and plain dates are taken as already local.

colors.description: `"github"`, a list of CSS colours (low to high, spread over the data), or a Scale (the same colours for the same values everywhere).

week_start.description: `"monday"` or `"sunday"`: the first row of the grid.

expected.description: A target per day, flagged when a day is below it (days with no data count as below): a number, a Series indexed by date, or a DataFrame with the `date` column, an `expected` column and, with `group`, the group column.

events.description: Dates to mark: a list of dates, or a DataFrame with `start` and optional `end`, `label` and `color` (a CSS colour; the accent by default) columns. A day is outlined and dotted, a span drawn as a band.

on_click.description: `"rows"` lists the rows behind a day in a panel when it is clicked (up to `ROWS_PER_CELL` per cell); `None` for none.

start.description: The first day shown (`"2026-05-19"` or a date), whatever the data covers; `None` starts at the first day with data or an event. Rows before it are left out, with a warning.

end.description: The last day shown; `None` ends at the last day with data or an event. Rows after it are left out, with a warning. Calendars with the same `start` and `end` line up week for week.

group_order.description: Group names to draw first, in this order (e.g. `["Worldwide", "United States"]`); other groups follow by name. Needs `group`; a name that isn't a group is an error.

legend.description: `False` hides this block's legend (show one Legend instead).

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

lab.TimeHeatmap.description: When something usually happens: a grid that crosses two units of one date column.

df.description: The data, as any dataframe briefing accepts (pandas, polars, pyarrow…).

date.description: Column holding the date or timestamp of each row.

rows.description: The unit down the side: `"hour"` (0–23), `"weekday"`, `"day"` (of the month), `"week"` (ISO week), `"month"`, `"quarter"` or `"year"`.

columns.description: The unit across the top, one of the same, and not the same as `rows`.

value.description: Column to aggregate per cell; `None` counts the rows.

agg.description: How to aggregate `value`: `"sum"`, `"mean"`, `"median"`, `"min"`, `"max"` or `"count"`. Sums and counts are averaged per occurrence.

group.description: Column to split by: one grid per group, stacked, on one shared colour scale.

tz.description: A time zone such as `"America/Montreal"`. Converts timezone-aware timestamps only; naive timestamps and plain dates are taken as already local.

colors.description: `"github"`, a list of CSS colours (low to high, spread over the data), or a Scale (the same colours for the same values everywhere).

week_start.description: `"monday"` or `"sunday"`: the first weekday of a `weekday` axis.

on_click.description: `"rows"` lists the rows behind a cell in a panel when it is clicked (up to `ROWS_PER_CELL` per cell); `None` for none.

group_order.description: Group names to draw first, in this order (e.g. `["Worldwide", "United States"]`); other groups follow by name. Needs `group`; a name that isn't a group is an error.

legend.description: `False` hides this block's legend (show one Legend instead).

name.description: Stable block id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`), its link in the report (`#page/name`).

label.description: Tab or dropdown label when the block is inside a `Select`.

name.description: A block's name: a letter, then letters, digits, _ or -. It is the block's link (#page/name) and unique within its page.

ref.description: An object passed separately, by name: from_spec(spec, data={name: object}). Any option can be one.

table.description: A table written into the JSON: column names, optional pandas dtypes (such as int64, float64, bool, object, datetime64[ns], category) and rows of values. Missing values are null; dates are ISO strings.

figure.description: A chart written into the JSON: a Plotly figure's JSON or a Vega-Lite specification (drawn with Altair). Matplotlib and Bokeh figures go by reference.

header.description: What the report header shows besides the name and render time (bf.Header); every key is optional. The logo is an image file's path or a data: URI; as_of is an ISO date or date and time.

scale.description: A colour scale (bf.Scale): hex colours low to high, mixed in OKLab; domain fixes the values they stand for ([low, high], or category names for a named palette), center makes it diverging, steps makes it classed.

chip.description: A pill with more than its text (bf.Chip): a tooltip, and a colour: up, down, accent or a CSS colour.

tab_style.description: How a row of tabs looks (bf.TabStyle); every key is optional.

image.description: An image file's path, or the image as a data: URI (data:image/png;base64,...).

file.description: A file's path, or its content as a data: URI (data:application/pdf;base64,...).

report.description: A briefing report as JSON: the same blocks and options as in Python. Build it with briefing.from_spec(spec, data) and check it with briefing.validate(spec, data).

briefing.description: The format version of this JSON (not briefing's version): 1.

export.description: Opt-in export menu in the report header: `"png"` adds "Save as PNG" (the open page with a margin around it, drawn in the reader's browser at 2×). Reports without it contain no export code. "Save as PNG" is best effort: charts drawn in iframes (Bokeh) and WebGL Plotly traces come out blank, and fonts are whatever the reader's machine has. For exact, reproducible files use save_image / save_pdf. To print, use the browser's own print (Ctrl+P or ⌘P): it gets the same print layout. `"embed"` puts a `</>` button on each page, labelled group, chart, table, text, number, alert and banner: it copies that part as an embed fragment, as stringify makes with `full_html=False`, to paste into another page. `"snapshot"` puts a camera button on the same blocks: it copies that block, as it is on screen, as a PNG image at 2× to the clipboard, ready to paste into a slide or a message, and downloads it when the clipboard is refused. It has the same limits as "Save as PNG". `"pdf"` (the "Print" button) was removed in 0.4.0: print with Ctrl+P, or save a file with save_pdf.

footer.description: Text to put before the report's footer line, such as a team name. Every report ends with "Made with briefing" and its version; that line can't be turned off.

tabs.description: How the page tabs look, for a report made of Page blocks: a TabStyle such as `bf.TabStyle(layout="stretch", sticky=True)`.

header.description: What the header shows besides the name and render time: a Header with a subtitle, author, logo, "data as of" date and time zone.

blocks.description: The report's blocks, in order: all of them Page blocks, or none.

deck.description: A briefing slide deck as JSON (bf.deck.Deck): its slides, each holding blocks. Build it with briefing.deck.from_spec(spec, data).

briefing.description: The format version of this JSON (not briefing's version): 1.

footer.description: Text before the "Made with briefing" line at the foot of every slide, such as a team name.

slide.description: One slide of a deck: a title over blocks stacked top to bottom, as in a report.

type.description: Optional: a slide is known by its place in "slides".

title.description: The slide's heading, with inline Markdown as in captions.

name.description: Stable slide id (letters, digits, `_` and `-`): its link in the deck (`#name`).

blocks.description: The slide's blocks, top to bottom.
